Figure 3: Discrete SID space landscape on two datasets. Each point denotes a tokenizer. The x-axis is inverse normalized Top-1 Load, and the y-axis is normalized Minimum Perplexity. Point size and color denote Mean Perplexity and SID Entropy. Points nearer the upper-right, and with larger and darker markers, indicate a more uniformly utilized and more diverse SID space.
Table 4: Ablation study of AdaSID on Toys and Beauty. The full model is boldfaced.

Figure 2: Overall framework of AdaSID. AdaSID maps collaborative trigger–target item pairs into quantized representations and Semantic IDs, and then optimizes them through a two-stage adaptive overlap regulation process: semantic-adaptive overlap relaxation first determines whether repulsion should be relaxed, after which load-adaptive collision strengthening and progress-adaptive objective rebalancing regulate the remaining overlaps across discrete regions and training time.
